subtype: Approach: pretending nothing happened and acting normal [Thinking]
passage: Ganga, come and sit. Your grandfather Francis once had a fight with his friend Anthony over a lost marble. I was ten. The next morning I said to myself: if I act as if nothing happened, maybe it will all melt away. So I walked up to Anthony at the gate and held out half a banana chip packet. "Want some?" Anthony took a chip and we chewed together. It worked, that day. But Anthony's eyes stayed on the ground, and he did not laugh at my jokes. Weeks later I learned he had been waiting for me to say something about the marble.

qa.q: What did Francis offer Anthony at the gate?
qa.a: Francis offered half a packet of banana chips.

qa.q: What did Francis want to happen when the chips were held out at the gate?
qa.a: Francis hoped that acting as if nothing had happened would make the fight melt away, which shows a wish to avoid an awkward talk.

qa.q: What choice inside the story could Francis have made differently, and why might it help?
qa.a: Francis could have mentioned the marble and said sorry along with sharing the chips, because saying it aloud would have shown that Anthony's hurt mattered.

qa.q: How did the sharing of chips feel to Anthony?
qa.a: It felt like a kind gesture but not enough; Anthony had been waiting for Francis to say something about the marble.

grounding: A child invites a friend to share a snack as if there was no fight, which works for a day but leaves the hurt unspoken.
